name: WATCHMAN / AIT-NEO
full_name: Water Cherenkov Monitor for Antineutrinos / Advanced Instrumentation Testbed–Neutrino Experiment One
summary: WATCHMAN studied remote reactor-antineutrino monitoring with a large water-based detector. The concept evolved from a United States design to the AIT/NEO proposal at Boulby in the United Kingdom. Full-scale Boulby deployment was subsequently questioned, while smaller technology-testbed work was discussed.
detection_principle: Inverse beta decay would produce a prompt positron signal and delayed neutron capture. Gadolinium loading enhances the neutron tag in water Cherenkov detection, while water-based scintillator and fast photosensors were considered for later performance improvements.

status.label: Historical proposal / full-scale realization unverified
status.evidence: The Boulby director’s April 2022 report states that the full AIT-NEO detector was unlikely to proceed at Boulby and describes smaller testbeds. An older future-tense institutional overview is not proof of construction or operation.

timeline.event: United States WATCHMAN design and physics white paper submitted
Boulby report says full AIT-NEO deployment is unlikely; smaller technology work discussed

results.summary: Published studies describe expected remote-monitoring and physics performance. A full-scale WATCHMAN/AIT-NEO reactor-neutrino measurement was not verified.
